results.original_text: As a site editor, I want to have pretty good control over how the article, so that articles are visually appealing.
results.final_text:
User Story:
As a site editor, I want to have comprehensive control over the formatting and layout of articles so that I can ensure they are visually engaging and align with our brand standards, enhancing reader retention.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Editors should be able to customize article layouts using at least 5 different formatting options, including font styles, colors, and image placements.
- The article preview must accurately reflect changes in real-time, with updates appearing within 2 seconds of modifications.
- At least 90% of readers should indicate that the visual appeal of articles positively impacts their reading experience in a follow-up survey.

Test Outline:
- Test the formatting tools by measuring the time taken to apply and preview changes to an article.
- Conduct reader surveys to gather feedback on the visual appeal of articles after applying various formatting options.

User Story:
As a site editor, I want to have comprehensive control over the formatting and layout of articles so that I can ensure they are visually appealing and engaging for readers.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Editors must be able to customize at least 10 different formatting options (e.g., font size, color, alignment) for each article.
- Articles should maintain a consistent visual style, achieving an 85% or higher satisfaction rating from readers in visual appeal surveys.
- The editing interface must allow for real-time changes, with updates reflected in the preview within 2 seconds.

Test Outline:
- Evaluate the article formatting features by testing the ability to apply various styles and measuring the time taken for changes to appear.
- Conduct reader surveys post-article publication to assess their feedback on the visual presentation and overall appeal of the articles.

history.text:
User Story:
As a site editor, I want to have comprehensive control over the article formatting and layout so that I can create visually appealing articles that enhance reader engagement and retention.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Editors should be able to customize article layouts with a minimum of 6 different formatting options (e.g., headings, images, bullet points) to choose from.
- The visual appeal of articles, as measured by user engagement metrics (e.g., average time spent on page), should improve by at least 20% after implementing the new control features.
- At least 90% of editors should report satisfaction with the formatting tools in a feedback survey.

Test Outline:
- Analyze user engagement metrics before and after the introduction of new formatting controls to quantify improvement.
- Conduct surveys with site editors to gather qualitative feedback on the usability and effectiveness of the formatting options provided.

results.original_text: I want a search bar on the top of the page.
results.final_text:
User Story:
As a website visitor, I want a search bar positioned at the top of the page so that I can quickly access information without scrolling or navigating through multiple menus.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The search bar must be visible and accessible on all pages, ensuring a consistent experience for 100% of users.
- Users should be able to initiate a search within 2 clicks, leading to results displayed in under 3 seconds for at least 90% of queries.
- At least 80% of users should report finding the search functionality intuitive and easy to use in follow-up surveys.

Test Outline:
- Verify the visibility of the search bar across different devices and screen sizes to ensure it meets design specifications.
- Analyze user interactions with the search bar to assess the time taken from input to results being displayed and gather feedback on usability.

history.text:
User Story:
As a website visitor, I want a search bar prominently placed at the top of the page so that I can easily locate content and navigate the site efficiently without unnecessary scrolling.

Acceptance Criteria:
- The search bar must be visible on the top of the page on all device screen sizes (≥ 95% of users should be able to see it without scrolling).
- The search bar should support instant search suggestions, displaying at least 5 relevant results as users type within 1 second.
- User engagement metrics should show a 30% increase in the use of the search feature within 3 months of implementation.

Test Outline:
- Verify the visibility of the search bar across multiple devices and screen resolutions to ensure consistent placement.
- Analyze user interaction data to measure the frequency of search feature usage before and after the search bar implementation.
